name: Anarcho-Syndicalism
summary: Anarcho-syndicalism is the anarchist wing of revolutionary trade unionism. It holds that unions, organised from below and federated, should wage the class struggle by direct action and the general strike, then take over production themselves and replace both capitalism and the state. It rejects parliaments, political parties and any dictatorship, and is internationalist and anti-militarist.
scope: The classical movement as theorised by Rudolf Rocker (Anarcho-Syndicalism, 1938) and practised by Spain's CNT, using its 1936 Zaragoza resolution on libertarian communism as the programme. It excludes plain syndicalism without the anarchist goal of abolishing the state, and Marxist-influenced union strategies.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Production and consumption are to be organised by labour councils and federations rather than competitive markets.

public-ownership.rationale: Industry is to be collectivised under workers' control by unions, not owned by the state, so public ownership in the usual sense is rejected.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are the vehicle of class struggle and the embryo of the new society.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Zaragoza resolution declares private property abolished after the revolution.

worker-ownership.rationale: Workers' control of production and distribution is the central economic aim.

strong-leader.rationale: Rocker rejects leaders, dictatorship and domination from above in favour of organisation from below.

state-harmful.rationale: Abolition of the state alongside capitalism is the stated goal.

limit-guns.rationale: The resolution favours an armed population ("the people armed") as protection of the revolution.

empower-police-military.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is not about military spending, which this statement now asks about alone.

reviewHistory.rationale: The resolution calls a permanent army the greatest danger to the revolution.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is not about military spending, which this statement now asks about alone.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

decide-locally.rationale: Rocker wants free combination from below upward and calls centralism a curse.

rehabilitation.rationale: The resolution rejects prisons and punitive institutions and blames crime on social injustice.

traditional-family.rationale: The family is not attacked, but free love and equality of the sexes replace traditional authority structures.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religion is tolerated only as private conscience, not public display or coercion.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Rocker holds that workers' interests cross borders and distrusts the nation state and its cultural claims.

gradual-change.rationale: Revolutionary change, with violent convulsions where necessary, is expected, and existing institutions are not respected.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Class solidarity across borders is a core principle.

nation-first.rationale: Workers should not tie their efforts to national states.

open-borders.rationale: Class interests cross borders and nation states are rejected.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Favours industrial production under workers' control but Rocker also notes machines reduced workers to mechanism parts.

revolution-justified.rationale: Rocker holds social transformation cannot come without violent revolutionary convulsions.

experts-over-public.rationale: Rocker warns against domination by bureaucratic mediocrity and stresses the creative energy of the masses.

central-planning.rationale: Coordination is by federations from below; centralism is rejected as a curse.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance goes with private property to be abolished, but taxing it presupposes a state; adherents split.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Rocker rejects the state as defender of privilege and wants economic direction by labour councils.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Rocker supports collectivising land and other means of production, not spreading private ownership.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Libertarian communism aims at distribution by need; production cards and some wages are transitional.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies are the opposite of free federations independent of the state.

one-party-rule.rationale: Rocker says party dictatorship became the rule of a small clique over the proletariat.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Rocker holds that the state defends privilege; monarchy is its extreme form.

democracy-best.rationale: Parliamentary democracy is called a failed expression of capitalism, though assemblies and self-management are favoured.

direct-votes.rationale: Popular assemblies and councils settle matters; the text rejects parliament.

workers-councils.rationale: Rocker names a system of labour councils as the political form of Socialism.

right-to-secede.rationale: Communes are autonomous within a federation and may opt out of general agreements.

war-builds-character.rationale: Workers should refuse to serve the wars of the possessing classes.

separate-church-state.rationale: Religion is a private matter, and the state is abolished anyway.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Religion is limited to private conscience and authority of any kind is rejected.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The Zaragoza text puts defence in an armed population and justice in popular assemblies, not companies.

military-superiority.rationale: The CNT's Zaragoza programme warns that 'a permanent army would constitute the greatest danger to the revolution' and entrusts defence to the armed people and the communes.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Nationalism is rejected in favour of cross-border class solidarity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Class struggle awakens worker solidarity and is the method of revolution, though Rocker rejects economic determinism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Distribution by need and equal rights for all point toward material equality.

civilizational-union.rationale: Unions of states or civilisations on religious lines contradict internationalism.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Solidarity and mutual agreement are the basis of their organisation.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rocker puts individual freedom first within free agreement and rejects imposed collective claims.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalism favours industrialisation, unlike primitivist currents.

restore-past-order.rationale: Revolutionary goals aim at a new society, not a lost one.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Rocker insists means must follow principle: socialism will be free or not at all.

direct-action.rationale: Strikes, boycotts and sabotage are used instead of legal channels and parliament.

means-match-ends.rationale: Rocker says socialism will be free or it will not be at all.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Favours industrial production under workers' control.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The resolution's first principle is giving each person what they need, though contribution is used transitionally.

production-for-use.rationale: Rocker contrasts cooperative labour serving needs with production for profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Rocker, drawing on Proudhon, sees property as the privilege of exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rocker calls it a frightful despotism that became a small clique's dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Rocker supports collectivising land, and rural collectives are discussed, though some communes opt out.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Rocker calls wars those of the possessing classes and criticises the scramble for markets.

conscription.rationale: Permanent armies and compulsion are rejected in favour of an armed population.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is a defender of privilege to be abolished, not run like a business.

positive-liberty.rationale: Rocker says higher cultural life and freedom need a material standard of living first.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Equality of rights and rejection of privilege; race science is not part of the doctrine.

organic-representation.rationale: Rejects parties but uses workplace councils and communes, not families or corporate bodies.

total-state.rationale: Rocker says state and culture are irreconcilable opposites.

national-rebirth.rationale: Rocker opposes nationalism and fascism's drive to bring all life under the state, implying rejection of national rebirth, which he does not discuss as such.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Rejects the state and nationalism; Rocker criticises seizing markets at others' cost.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rejecting every form of political power and privilege excludes feudal loyalty, though Rocker does not discuss oaths of fealty.

bound-labor.rationale: Rocker praises the uprisings of feudal bondmen peasants for preparing the abolition of feudal privileges, treating serfdom as domination to be overthrown.

single-common-good.rationale: Rocker criticises the abstract general will and favours free agreement among groups.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers run plants through labour councils elected by them.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: State fiscal policy is outside their programme; adherents split.

national-self-determination.rationale: Workers should not tie themselves to national states; free communes are the unit instead.

force-without-un.rationale: Opposes wars of states and militarism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Class solidarity across borders rejects citizenship-based exclusion.

class-collaboration.rationale: Class struggle through unions is the method; collaboration is rejected.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Rocker values culture and calls for a material base for it, not its destruction.

workers-nation.rationale: Rocker says workers' solidarity 'must reach beyond the artificial boundaries of the states' and that labour must not tie its efforts 'with the interests of the national states'.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The text declares the sexes equal in rights and responsibilities.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Rocker calls the state the defender of mass exploitation and social privileges.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Cross-border solidarity and rejection of nationalism make cultural assimilation demands foreign.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy of this kind is not part of the doctrine, which stresses class solidarity across borders.

national-mission.rationale: Rocker condemns socialists who backed annexations in the World War and opposes national states, implying rejection of any national mission abroad.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The text ties women's dependence to capitalism and demands equal rights.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Rocker says party ambition for power corrupted Socialism.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Rocker calls the state 'capable only of protecting old privileges and creating new ones' and 'the defender of mass exploitation and social privileges', so a state that protects property is what he rejects.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The text declares the sexes equal in rights and responsibilities and rejects privilege.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The state is rejected; equality before the law is not the question for them.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Religion is for individual conscience, which excludes coercion.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Education is to be free, scientific and equal; religion is private.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Rocker rejects the idea that the state withers after being strengthened.

separated-powers.rationale: They would abolish the state rather than balance it; federations of councils replace it.

vanguard-party.rationale: Rocker says a party speaking for a class becomes a clique's dictatorship.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The strike and the general strike are the central weapons.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Rocker defends rights as habit defended by the people and distrusts state power.

party-controls-media.rationale: Rocker condemns Bolshevik rule as 'the dictatorship of a small clique', implying opposition to party control of information, though he does not discuss the press.

party-commands-army.rationale: Rocker rejects party dictatorship; permanent army is rejected.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Rocker accepts violent upheaval and armed resistance as part of revolution, and their goals do not rest on non-aggression.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Wikipedia notes delegates serve single terms and are paid the same as the workers they represent.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The movement rejects the state and standing armies in favor of an armed population, so a head of state commanding the military is opposed.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The CNT program and Rocker reject church authority and hierarchy.

clerical-rule.rationale: The CNT program and Rocker reject religious authority over society and the state.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Rocker opposed militarism, but revolutionary defeatism is a Leninist line; in 1914 the French CGT backed the war while the IWW opposed it, and the CNT joined the Republican war effort in 1936, so the movement is split.

recall-officials.rationale: Delegates are mandated and revocable by the bodies that send them in the federal union structure.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists are outspoken opponents of nationalist ambitions and militarism and fight war through anti-militarist propaganda and strikes.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Rocker describes the movement as hostile to all nationalist ambitions, so it would not seek to unify nations in states.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The movement distrusts intellectual leaders but the 1936 program stresses universal education; adherents are split.

death-penalty.rationale: The Zaragoza program declares libertarian communism incompatible with punitive justice, abolishing prisons, and attributes crime to social causes.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The Zaragoza program calls for free, scientific education equal for both sexes, with sex education beginning at school.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The program wants scientific education and confines religion to private conscience, so creationism in schools is excluded.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Rocker holds that political freedom from the state means little without ending capitalist ownership, and criticises nationalism as serving ruling classes.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Rocker rejects parliaments and the state and favours federated labour councils, so a state constituent assembly is not their route.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists reject dictatorship and any state coercion in the name of development, as Rocker condemns the Bolshevik path.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Rocker rejects the state, parliament and parties, so a president elected by the people has no place.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Rocker rejects nationalism and the national state, and the movement is internationalist.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The Zaragoza programme puts production and property in common ownership for the needs of all.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Rocker condemns Bolshevism as a state dictatorship over workers that kept hierarchy and wage labour.

collective-defense.rationale: Rocker opposes militarism and nationalism, and the CNT favoured an armed population in place of standing armies and alliances.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Rocker rejects the state and its offices and parties in favour of federated labour bodies.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Rocker's federalism builds from voluntary association from below and rejects the coercive nation-state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Rocker rejects the state and all forms of rule, and the CNT programme rejects religious authority.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rocker opposes any rule above the people, which a sovereign above law embodies.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Rocker rejects government by the few and parliamentary rule in favour of federated councils.

leader-cult.rationale: Rocker rejects dictatorship, leader worship and authority from above.

equal-parenting.rationale: The CNT programme addresses family and education but not custody rules; no clear position.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Zaragoza program calls for expropriating land and its collective use by the working peasants.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Rocker's anarcho-syndicalism is internationalist and rejects nationalism.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The movement was secular and strongly anticlerical.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalism is internationalist and opposes unity by nationality.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The movement is internationalist and opposes closed economic blocs and colonialism.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The strategy is the mass general strike and union action, not a small armed group.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Libertarian communism abolishes class privilege, including inherited rank.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rocker condemns the state and national domination and the movement is anti-imperialist, so one society ruling another for its good is rejected.

patriotic-education.rationale: Rocker sees nationalism and the state's claim on loyalty as tools of power, and the CNT programme demands education free of state and church control.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Rocker opposes nationalism, power politics and the state's expansion, so cultivating influence over a predecessor empire's lands is rejected.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The movement's equality of all people and rejection of domination mean it would not defend discrimination by owners; the CNT also rejects private property in production.

minority-veto.rationale: Federal free agreement stresses voluntary association and the right to withdraw, but union decisions are taken by majority; adherents split.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Adherents split between vegetarian abolitionists and those who accept humane use; the sources are silent.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Rocker's movement demands active participation in social struggle and self-management, although it rejects parliamentary politics.

native-born-offices.rationale: Rocker rejects nationalism, and the movement is internationalist and wants no state offices to reserve in the first place.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Rocker rejects nationalism and the movement is internationalist and anti-militarist, so territorial claims are rejected.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Rocker condemns Bolshevik dictatorship alongside fascism, and the movement was crushed by both Franco and Stalinists.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Rocker's movement is anti-militarist and rejects any standing army or military power.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Delegates serve a single term, are paid as workers and can be recalled, which matches mandated delegation.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The programme replaces wages with distribution by need under communes, so private pension accounts are rejected.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The 1936 resolution places land and production in the communes and producers' bodies; the nation is not their unit.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Rocker attacks militarism, imperialism and Bolshevik domination, so military intervention within a bloc is rejected.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Rocker rejects the state's authority and its law as instruments of ruling-class power, so no general duty to obey the law.

non-intervention.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists oppose states, but supported international solidarity as in the Spanish Civil War; adherents would split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalism organises workers in industrial federations of unions, as the CNT did, rather than by craft.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Rocker rejects nationalism and racism in favour of internationalism.

local-production.rationale: The CNT programme has communes federated and exchanging goods, so local production is partial but not a stated principle.

informal-organisation.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalism relies on permanent federated unions, not informal groups.

religious-nation.rationale: The CNT programme rejects religion and Rocker rejects nationalism, so a nation defined by religion contradicts it.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists see capitalism as a stage that concentrated production but stress its exploitation; adherents are split and the sources do not settle it.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The programme is built on federated free communes owning means of production in common.

majority-settlement.rationale: Rocker rejects nationalism and state policy to assimilate peoples, so state-steered settlement is opposed.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Rocker rejects both capitalism and Bolshevik state communism in favour of federal, union-run socialism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Anarchists are internationalist and reject nations and states as the bearers of rights, so a people's tie to land does not outrank the claims of those living there now.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Rejecting state coercion over personal life and the criminal law as an instrument of authority, adherents oppose criminalising consensual relations.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Suppressing opposition is the practice of the state and dictatorship that the ideology rejects, and it criticised the Bolsheviks for exactly this.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Adherents are anti-clerical and oppose any state enforcing religion; punishing blasphemy would be authority at its worst.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Anti-imperialism and internationalism follow from rejecting exploitation and the state; colonial rule for the ruler's benefit is exploitation.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Direct self-management by those affected, in workplaces and communities through federated assemblies, is the core of the ideology's alternative to the state.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The ideology sits firmly on the revolutionary left and sees capitalists and workers as opposed classes whose best ideas cannot be merged.

alienated-labor.rationale: Wage labour is condemned as wage slavery that cuts workers off from the product and control of their work, and free creative work is the aim.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Atheism and the rejection of all authority are central, as in Bakunin's anarchist critique of God and the state.

social-market-economy.rationale: Both markets and wage relations are rejected, and the state-regulated compromise is rejected as well; production and distribution are to be organised in common.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Anti-militarism is central and the standing army is rejected, but the movement organised its own militias in 1936; so agreement is strong but not total.

rich-first.rationale: Equality and abolition of class privilege are central; letting some get rich first contradicts them.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Anti-militarism and rejection of rival states point to refusing alignment with great-power blocs, though adherents would prefer no state armies at all.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists reject the state and all hereditary authority; Rocker treats monarchy and privilege as products of power to be abolished.

property-franchise.rationale: Rocker rejects parliamentary politics and class privilege, so a property qualification on voting is opposed on both counts.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists hold that political freedoms are empty under capitalism, and they built their own union press because the owners' press was closed to them.

racial-franchise.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalism is internationalist and organises workers regardless of race, so it opposes ethnic limits on rights.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The movement was strongly anticlerical and opposed state and church control of private life, so it rejects legal limits on marriage.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists see capitalist ownership as the root of class domination and want productive wealth held by the unions and communes, so concentrated wealth is a threat to liberty.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The movement wants the state abolished, so a state programme of promoting atheism conflicts with its principles, even though the CNT and many members were anticlerical.

term-limits.rationale: Wikipedia notes that delegates serve single terms and are paid the same as the workers they represent, which is rotation of office.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Rocker rejects nationalism, militarism and state-run organisation of the young, so drilled youth movements for national service are the opposite of the programme.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Rocker's anti-militarism and rejection of the state's armed power make stationing nuclear weapons on any territory unacceptable.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The movement is anti-militarist and internationalist and opposes state armies, so foreign bases are opposed, though not in the language of national sovereignty.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Zaragoza programme replaces property income with production cards for useful work and abolishes rent and interest as unearned.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The programme calls for an armed population to defend the revolution and Rocker accepts defensive revolutionary force, so adherents do not hold that all killing is wrong.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Rocker argues that nations are products of the state and of ruling-class interests, not a continuous ancient essence.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Rocker rejects nationalism and the cult of the nation, so sacralising the national dead is rejected.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Zaragoza programme is materialist and treats religion as a private matter, and Rocker sees politics as class struggle, not a cosmic one.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Rocker's internationalism and class view reject tying economic life to national majority groups.

independent-unions.rationale: Rocker holds that unions must stay independent of parties and the state, and the profile's own missing statement records the same position.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Rocker treats socialism without workers' own self-management as state capitalism, though he wants workers to hold power through councils and unions rather than a political state.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The Zaragoza programme has communes and syndicates run services such as health and education collectively, which is public ownership without the state.

municipal-property.rationale: The Zaragoza programme makes the commune the basic unit that holds and administers productive property alongside the syndicates, rather than private owners or a national state.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Rocker's federalism builds from local bodies upward with delegates who coordinate and carry out decisions made below, which the statement describes.

person-over-state.rationale: Rocker puts the free development of the individual against the state's claims and sees the state as the enemy of personal liberty.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Rocker stresses culture and the free development of personality while the Zaragoza programme rejects organised religion, so adherents are split on this wording.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Federal autonomy for communes is meant to come from below and not be a grant from a national legislature, which anarcho-syndicalists reject as an authority.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Rocker rejects nationalism and group identity as divisions that serve rulers, and organises on class lines.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The movement is anti-militarist and opposes wars of states, while the Zaragoza programme keeps an armed population to defend the revolution.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Rocker argues the nation is the result of the state rather than its cause, and the movement is internationalist, so a nation defined by language and history is rejected.

communal-electorates.rationale: They reject parliament and elections and treat religion as private, so religious separate electorates are firmly opposed.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Rocker criticises nationalism and national defence as tools of ruling classes, so claims of plots against the country are dismissed.

free-public-college.rationale: The Zaragoza programme calls for universal education for all, though run by communes and unions rather than the state.

arms-reduction.rationale: Rocker condemns militarism and the CNT opposes standing armies, so lowering arms agrees in direction even though they reject national safety as the test.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists reject the state, and the CNT organised armed workers' militias in 1936.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Rocker's anti-militarism calls for refusing war service and for general strikes against war.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Unions are the core of the movement, though they pursue direct action and abolition of wage labour rather than negotiated contracts as the end.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Rocker holds the state must be replaced by federated workers' organisations, not taken over by parties.

sacred-nation.rationale: Rocker criticises nationalism as a tool of the state and the movement is internationalist and secular.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Rocker stresses human freedom and social development rather than a fixed nature; not directly addressed, adherents split.

workers-own-party.rationale: Rocker argues party participation drained socialism of its creative force and calls parliamentary activity the weakest form of struggle, favouring unions instead.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Rocker opposes state churches and clerical power, so no interpretation of a religion should hold legal privilege.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The movement rejects parliamentary politics as domination and defines real self-rule as direct, federated control from below, not periodic elections.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The Zaragoza programme puts land and production under communal and producers' control, rejecting private ownership.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Rocker rejects state socialism and any dictatorship, so a bureaucratic planned state is not to be defended.

indirect-election.rationale: The confederal model builds from local unions and communes upward through delegates who carry mandates from below.

equal-conscription.rationale: Anti-militarism is a core commitment, so the movement rejects conscription for everyone.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Rocker treats nationalism as a political religion serving rulers and the movement is internationalist.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The Zaragoza programme rejects prisons and state punishment and Rocker opposes state violence, so killing without trial is rejected.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The Zaragoza programme puts land and means of production in common through communes and union bodies, so users owe society rather than owning outright.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists reject party leaders but rely on federated unions and labour councils, so bypassing organised groups is opposed.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The Zaragoza programme is anticlerical and Rocker opposes church power in public life, though they also reject offices.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The Zaragoza programme treats family as a free union and equality of the sexes, so either partner may end it.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The CNT programme distributes by need and rejects private accumulation, so it judges fairness by outcomes and exploitation rather than by process alone.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Rocker rejects nationalism as an instrument of the state and of the ruling classes that divides workers.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Rocker rejects party leadership and the state, and the CNT programme abolishes the market and money, so a party-led market economy contradicts it.

missingStatements.text: A general strike is the best way to bring down capitalism.
missingStatements.rationale: Rocker calls the general strike a political action of greater importance than parliamentary proceedings, and Wikipedia names it as the key moment of revolution.

missingStatements.text: Trade unions should remain independent of all political parties.
missingStatements.rationale: Rocker argues party participation drained socialism of its creative force and calls parliamentary activity the weakest form of struggle.

missingStatements.text: Elected representatives should be paid no more than an average worker.
missingStatements.rationale: Wikipedia notes that delegates serve single terms and are paid the same as the workers they represent.

notes: The CNT joined the Republican government in 1936, which was controversial within the anarcho-syndicalist international. Distribution is disputed: some supporters keep contribution-based pay in a transition, others stress need. Ecology, religion and money are thinly covered by the sources read.
